summary:
The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia because of the threat of Houthi attacks on the kingdom. The order comes as at least three people died in recent strikes: two at a Saudi Aramco facility and one at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. Brent crude rose more than 2% to above $111 a barrel as traders weighed the attacks and the risk of further US-Iran hostilities.

Moscow said it was 'ready in principle' to resume peace talks, and Zelenskyy said Ukraine supported a US proposal for three-way talks at negotiator level, preferably no later than early November. Russia and Ukraine nonetheless traded major attacks, and Ukrainian authorities said seven people were killed on their side overnight. Russia also freed the American Stephen Hubbard, who had been jailed for four years, during talks between Putin and Steve Witkoff.

A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company deceived users, in a case linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. The ruling follows an $18 billion settlement with 48 other states over similar claims. The Vatican said Wednesday that Pope Leo XIV, 71, will need no further lung cancer treatment after tests showed the disease was localized.

headlines.title: US orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi threat
headlines.summary: The State Department has ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia over the threat of Houthi attacks. The order follows strikes that killed at least three people at an airport and an oil field.

headlines.title: Oil rises above $111 a barrel after attacks in Saudi Arabia
headlines.summary: Brent crude rose more than 2% to above $111 a barrel as traders weighed renewed attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. A strike on a Saudi Aramco facility killed two people, and an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one.

headlines.title: Russia agrees to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and US
headlines.summary: Moscow said it was 'ready in principle' to resume talks, and Zelenskyy backed a US proposal for three-way talks at negotiator level, preferably by early November. Russia also freed American Stephen Hubbard, jailed for four years, during Putin's talks with Witkoff.

headlines.title: Russia and Ukraine trade major attacks after Witkoff talks
headlines.summary: Russian attacks killed one person and injured 22 in Kyiv, and Ukrainian authorities said seven people were killed on their side overnight. The strikes came shortly after Putin and Zelenskyy expressed willingness to resume US-mediated talks.

headlines.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion in New Mexico Cambridge Analytica case
headlines.summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a $25 billion civil penalty after a jury found it deceived users in a case linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. The ruling follows an $18 billion settlement with 48 other states over similar claims.

headlines.title: Pope Leo needs no further lung cancer treatment, Vatican says
headlines.summary: The Vatican said Wednesday that Pope Leo XIV, 71, will need no further treatment for lung cancer after tests confirmed the disease was localized. He had part of his right lung removed last week after being diagnosed with adenocarcinoma.

headlines.title: Drone strike on Abyei market kills more than 150, officials say
headlines.summary: The death toll from a drone strike on Amiet market in the disputed Abyei area rose from 73 to 153, local officials said. They expect it to grow, as many people are still listed as missing.

headlines.title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case, a diplomat's wife who visited Uganda
headlines.summary: Nigerian health authorities confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja, the country's first, and Africa CDC said the patient is a diplomat's wife who had holidayed in Uganda. The aviation minister, Keyamo, has ordered 46 of the woman's contacts onto a 21-day no-fly list.
